label: Genetic Peroxisomal Disorders
summary: Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders (PBDs) including Zellweger Spectrum Disorder (ZSD), and single-enzyme or transporter disorders such as X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD)
description: Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders (PBDs) including Zellweger Spectrum Disorder (ZSD), and single-enzyme or transporter disorders such as X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD).

parts.label: Zellweger Spectrum Disorders (Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders)
parts.text: Variants in any one of more than a dozen PEX genes hinder peroxisomes from forming or importing their enzymes. Severity ranges from death in infancy to milder forms that enable individuals to reach adulthood.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** variants in PEX genes hinder peroxisomes from forming or importing their enzymes, causing broad peroxisomal dysfunction.
**Diagnosis:** raised VLCFAs, low plasmalogens, raised 27-carbon bile acid intermediates and phytanic/pristanic acid in blood, now usually confirmed by gene panel or whole exome sequencing.
**Treatment:** no disease-modifying therapy and care is supportive (e.g., oral cholic acid for bile acid intermediates, fat-soluble vitamins, hearing and vision support, and adrenal monitoring).
furtherReading: [Braverman 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26750748/) (clinical consensus guideline)
[Wanders 2018a](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mcp.2018.02.001) (improved laboratory diagnosis of peroxisomal disorders)
[Wanders 2018b](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-13-2233-4_15) (peroxisomes in metabolic interaction networks)
right: Therapies that restore import in specific variants, such as small-molecule chaperones for missense variants like PEX1-G843D ([MacLean 2019](https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.0914960107)) and gene therapy approaches tested in mouse retina ([Argyriou 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8516995/)).

Whether manipulating pexophagy can preserve peroxisomal function in patients, now with a candidate target: inhibiting USP2 restored peroxisomes in PEX1 patient cells and improved movement in flies ([Kim 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42778528/)).
Structure-guided therapy: high-resolution structures of the import machinery ([Feng 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35768507/)) make it possible to ask which patient variants could be rescued.
Natural history data and validated blood biomarkers to make clinical trials feasible.

parts.label: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD)
parts.text: The most common peroxisomal disorder, caused by loss of ABCD1, the transporter that carries VLCFAs into peroxisomes. It causes adrenal insufficiency and spinal cord disease, and in some boys and men it also damages the brain. Women who carry one affected copy may develop spinal cord symptoms later in life.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** VLCFAs build up in blood and tissue, causing adrenal insufficiency, progressive spinal cord disease in adults (adrenomyeloneuropathy); and cerebral ALD, a rapid inflammatory loss of brain white matter, most often in boys.

**[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** losing ABCD1, the transporter behind X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, makes oligodendrocytes more vulnerable to a demyelinating insult in mice, accelerating oligodendrocyte loss and axon damage ([Martinović 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37331971/))
**[Immune & Inflammatory Signaling](#/mechanisms/immune-signaling):** microglial damage precedes demyelination in cerebral ALD ([Bergner 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30980503/)).

**Treatment:** cerebral ALD caught early is treated by stem cell transplant or the gene therapy elivaldogene autotemcel, which received FDA accelerated approval in 2022 ([Duncan 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39383458/)).
furtherReading: [Engelen 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22889154/) (clinical overview of X-ALD, from presentation to management)
[Martinović 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37331971/) (ABCD1 loss accelerates demyelination and axon damage)
right: Predicting which boys will develop cerebral disease, so treatment can be timed before damage starts.
Disease-modifying treatment for adult spinal cord disease (e.g., the PPARγ agonist leriglitazone has been studied in clinical trials).

parts.label: Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata (RCDP)
parts.text: A group of disorders in which plasmalogen synthesis fails, causing shortening of the upper arms and thighs (rhizomelia, the feature the disorder is named for), cataracts, skeletal changes and severe developmental delay from birth.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** RCDP type 1 is an import disorder limited to PTS2 cargo, which is why plasmalogen synthesis and phytanic acid breakdown fail while most other functions are spared.
**[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** caused by variants in peroxisomal genes that block plasmalogen synthesis.

Residual plasmalogen levels track with clinical severity: red blood cell plasmalogens are almost undetectable in classic RCDP, and higher residual levels in nonclassic forms correlate with better growth and development ([Fallatah 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33337545/)).
furtherReading: [Braverman 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22627108/) (clinical and biochemical overview of RCDP)
right: Whether plasmalogen replacement or synthetic plasmalogen precursors can raise tissue levels and improve outcomes. Dietary alkyl-glycerol restores plasmalogens and improves pathology in Pex7 knockout mice, but this work is preclinical ([Brites 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22163031/)).
Natural history studies and outcome measures for trials.

parts.label: Refsum disease
parts.text: Phytanic acid, a branched fat from the diet, cannot be broken down and slowly accumulates, causing vision loss, loss of smell, nerve damage and unsteady gait.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** caused by variants in PHYH (most cases) or PEX7.

**Treatment:** one of the few peroxisomal disorders with an effective intervention: restricting dietary phytanic acid, with plasma exchange in acute episodes ([Wanders 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21683154/)).
furtherReading: [Wanders 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21683154/) (phytanic acid metabolism and Refsum disease)
right: Earlier diagnosis, since retinal damage is largely irreversible by the time it is recognized.

parts.label: Single-enzyme disorders
parts.text: Loss of a single peroxisomal enzyme or tether disables one pathway, while the peroxisomes themselves form normally.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** D-bifunctional protein deficiency and ACOX1 deficiency cause severe infantile disease resembling severe Zellweger Spectrum Disorder; AMACR and ACOX2 deficiencies affect branched fats and bile acids.
**[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification):** primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (AGXT) causes kidney stones and kidney failure; lumasiran is approved for it.
**[Organelle Crosstalk](#/mechanisms/organelle-crosstalk):** ACBD5 deficiency, loss of a peroxisome-ER tether, causes retinal and white matter disease.
furtherReading: [Waterham 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26611709/) (genetics of peroxisomal disorders, biogenesis and single-enzyme)
right: Since each disorder isolates a single peroxisomal function, systematic comparison could show which functions drive which symptoms.

label: Cancer
summary: Prostate, colorectal, blood and brain tumors appear to rely on peroxisomal fat metabolism, ether lipid production, antioxidant capacity and protein import to grow and resist treatment
description: Prostate, colorectal, blood and brain tumors appear to rely on peroxisomal fat metabolism, ether lipid production, antioxidant capacity and protein import to grow and resist treatment.

parts.label: Tumors that run on peroxisomal fat burning
parts.panelTitle: Tumors that run on peroxisomal fat burning
parts.text: Several cancers raise the peroxisomal enzymes and transporters that break down fats, using them to fuel growth and to survive treatment.
left: **AMACR ([Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown)):** an established diagnostic marker for prostate cancer ([Luo 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11956072/); [Rubin 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11926890/)), separately linked to tumor growth and redox stress ([Kong 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32760737/)).

**DECR2 ([Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown)):** a second peroxisomal fat-burning enzyme that prostate tumors use to fuel growth and resist androgen-deprivation (hormone) therapy ([Mah 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41416-023-02557-8)).

**PMP70 ([Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown)):** PMP70 (ABCD3) protects drug-resistant colorectal cancer cells from toxic fat build-up and helps them evade treatment ([Yin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41419-025-07572-6)).

**ABCD1 ([Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown)):** acute myeloid leukemia cells raise ABCD1 (the transporter that carries very long chain fatty acids into the peroxisome), and run more peroxisomal fat burning than healthy blood-forming cells; blocking ABCD1 with eicosenol killed AML cells in culture and in mice (while normal blood-forming cells stayed viable), reducing leukemia burden and prolonging survival ([Parfenova 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41746867/)).
furtherReading: [Mah 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41416-023-02557-8) (tumors use DECR2 to burn fatty acids and resist hormone therapy)
[Kong 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32760737/) (AMACR links peroxisomal lipid metabolism to tumor growth and redox stress)
[Yin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41419-025-07572-6) (PMP70 protects drug-resistant colorectal cancer from toxic fat damage)
[Parfenova 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41746867/) (AML cells depend on ABCD1-driven peroxisomal fat burning; blocking it kills them selectively)
right: What molecular mechanism kills cancer cells when DECR2 is blocked, and does this directly inhibit hormone-driven survival?
In AMACR-high tumors, is there a specific dependency on peroxisomal AMACR activity, and does AMACR inhibition work together with anti-cancer PPAR antagonists?
Is PMP70's role in drug resistance about transporting fatty acids, or about positioning peroxisomes near lipid droplets?
Losing ABCD1 is also what causes X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, so how wide is the therapeutic window between killing leukemia cells and causing that harm?
When does PPAR activation help the host, and when does it help tumors or viruses? Can the harmful peroxisome-dependent part be blocked selectively?

parts.label: Lymphoma
parts.text: Peroxisomes buffer drug-induced free radicals, helping lymphoma cells survive otherwise lethal treatment.
left: **[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification):** peroxisomes buffer free radicals generated by cancer drugs in lymphoma; in the study cited, these were HDAC inhibitors (a class of cancer drug), specifically vorinostat ([Dahabieh 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5635217/)).
furtherReading: [Dahabieh 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5635217/) (peroxisomes buffer free radicals from chemotherapy in lymphoma)
[Dahabieh 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbcan.2018.07.004) (peroxisomes and cancer: a metabolic specialist in a disease of aberrant metabolism)
[Kim 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/cells9071692) (peroxisome metabolism in cancer)
right: Can lymphoma drug resistance be overcome by blocking peroxisomal antioxidants alone, or do multiple peroxisomal functions need to be targeted?
Can catalase or plasmalogen synthesis alone restore resistance to HDAC inhibitors?

parts.label: Ether lipid-dependent tumors (multiple types)
parts.text: The peroxisomal enzyme AGPS builds ether lipids that fuel cancer cell migration, invasion and survival across multiple tumor types.
left: **[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** AGPS-made ether lipids drive aggressive tumor behavior ([Chen 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51489-1)).
**[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** the same peroxisome-dependent ether lipids can make cancer cells more vulnerable to ferroptosis (Zou 2020).
furtherReading: [Chen 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51489-1) (AGPS-made ether lipids fuel cancer migration, invasion and survival)
right: Which AGPS-made lipids drive cancer aggression?
Do those same lipids make tumors vulnerable to ferroptosis-inducing treatment?
In cancer, can peroxisomal ROS buffering be deliberately disrupted to resensitize tumors to chemotherapy?

parts.label: Glioblastoma
parts.text: An aggressive primary brain tumor, glioma cells appear to depend on peroxisomal protein import and fat burning to grow and invade.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)**: PEX5, the receptor that carries enzymes into the peroxisome, is required for glioma cell growth, migration and invasion, and a peroxisomal enzyme signature carries prognostic information ([Qin 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38540734/)).
furtherReading: [Qin 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38540734/) (PEX5 is required for glioma cell growth, migration and invasion; the growth effect of the antioxidant enzyme GSTK1 depends on PTS1-mediated import)
right: What other peroxisome proteins are required for glioma cell growth?

label: Infection
summary: Many unrelated viruses have evolved to disable peroxisomes, blocking the cell's earliest antiviral response
description: Many unrelated viruses have evolved to disable peroxisomes, blocking the cell's earliest antiviral response.

parts.label: Viruses that reduce peroxisome numbers
parts.text: Flaviviruses, such as Zika and dengue, reduce peroxisome numbers, blunting early immune detection, and similar effects have been reported for other viruses including HIV and SARS-CoV-2.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling:](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)** these viruses reduce peroxisome numbers or disrupt key biogenesis factors to silence the peroxisomal MAVS-interferon alarm ([Knoblach 2021](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.E21-02-0074)). Influenza A does this directly: its M2 protein binds PEX19 and disrupts peroxisome formation, raising reactive oxygen species in a way that favors viral replication ([Liu 2024](https://www.mdpi.com/1999-4915/16/8/1309)).

**[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** infection reshapes peroxisome size, number and positioning over time ([Knoblach 2021](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.E21-02-0074)).
furtherReading: [You 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26423946/) (flaviviruses, such as Zika and dengue)
[Xu 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28594894/) (HIV)
[Knoblach 2021](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.E21-02-0074) (SARS-CoV-2)
[Liu 2024](https://www.mdpi.com/1999-4915/16/8/1309) (Influenza A)
right: Do viruses benefit more from reducing peroxisome numbers by shutting down immune signaling, or by rewiring lipid and stress metabolism to help replication?
Do viruses that chronically destroy peroxisomes contribute to accelerated aging or metabolic complications in infected patients?
How do changes in peroxisome number and shape track with function (fat breakdown, ROS handling, immune signaling) across tissues and diseases?

parts.label: Viruses that expand and exploit peroxisomes
parts.panelTitle: Viruses that expand and exploit peroxisomes
parts.text: Some viruses, including certain herpesviruses, expand peroxisomes and use them as factories for the lipids that build viral membranes.
left: **[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** some viruses deliberately expand peroxisomes to sustain replication, taking over ether lipid and plasmalogen production ([Ferreira 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34696946/)).

**[Organelle Crosstalk](#/mechanisms/organelle-crosstalk):** different viruses use peroxisomes in opposite ways: some destroy them to escape immunity, others expand them to take lipids and replication machinery ([Cook 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6857447/)).
furtherReading: [Ferreira 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34696946/) (review of how viruses expand and exploit peroxisomes)
[Cook 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6857447/) (peroxisome plasticity at the virus-host interface)
right: Which specific peroxisomal functions switch from protecting cells to helping viruses, and what determines that switch?
Which viral proteins directly grab peroxisomal machinery, and does the change in peroxisome shape itself alter how they work?
Do all viruses use the same remodeling playbook, or does each reprogram peroxisomes differently?

label: Brain, Nerve & Sensory Disease
summary: Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease all involve changes in the fats that peroxisomes build; when peroxisomal functions fail, the result is a loss of nerve insulation, vision and hearing
description: Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease all involve changes in the fats that peroxisomes build; when peroxisomal functions fail, the result is a loss of nerve insulation, vision and hearing.

parts.label: Alzheimer's disease
parts.text: Peroxisomal fat breakdown and plasmalogen synthesis fail in Alzheimer's brain tissue, and PPARγ drugs improve cognition in animal models.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown) and [Lipid Synthesis](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** VLCFA oxidation and plasmalogen synthesis fail in Alzheimer's brains ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)).

**[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification) and [Import](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** PEX5 import defects and catalase loss compromise ROS detoxification in neurodegenerative disease ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Metabolic Signaling](#/mechanisms/metabolic-signaling):** PPARγ agonists rescue cognition in animal models, but a peroxisome-driven mechanism is unproven ([Steinke 2023](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/12/8/1116)).

**[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** in Alzheimer's brains, peroxisomes build up in nerve cell bodies as pathology advances, while disappearing from the projections that carry abnormal tau, where mitochondria are left largely intact ([Kou 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21594711/)).

**[Lipid Breakdown:](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown)** peroxisome changes appear in an Alzheimer's mouse model before symptoms ([Cimini 2009](https://doi.org/10.3233/jad-2009-1199)), and blocking peroxisomal beta-oxidation in rats raises VLCFAs and amyloid-beta ([Shi 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neulet.2012.08.086)).
**[Detoxification:](#/mechanisms/detoxification)** peroxisome-targeted catalase protected rat neurons from amyloid-beta damage ([Giordano 2014](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep04983)).
furtherReading: [Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/) (VLCFA oxidation and plasmalogen synthesis fail in Alzheimer's and MS brains)
[Steinke 2023](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/12/8/1116) (PPARγ agonists rescue cognition in Alzheimer's models)
[Jo 2019](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12272-019-01131-2) (peroxisomal dysfunction in neurodegenerative disease)
[Kou 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21594711/) (peroxisomal alterations in Alzheimer's disease)
[Santos 2005](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.m505160200) (peroxisome proliferation protects neurons from amyloid-beta)
right: Does the benefit of PPARγ drugs require functional peroxisomal import and lipid metabolism?
Which plasmalogen and/or ether lipid species are most tightly linked to cognitive resilience versus decline?
Can restoring peroxisomal protein import alone slow or reverse neurodegeneration?
Can peroxisome-biased PPAR drugs keep the metabolic and brain-protective benefits while reducing side effects elsewhere in the body?

parts.label: Multiple sclerosis (MS)
parts.text: Peroxisomal lipid handling fails in MS brains, and in mice a peroxisomal transporter defect makes myelin-forming cells more vulnerable to a demyelinating insult, suggesting a route by which peroxisomal failure could contribute to multiple sclerosis.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling:](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)** neuronal peroxisomes are reduced in the grey matter of people with MS ([Gray 2014](https://doi.org/10.1177/1352458513505691)).

**[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown) and [Lipid Synthesis](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** VLCFA oxidation and plasmalogen synthesis fail in MS brains, disrupting myelin integrity ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)).

**[Organelle Crosstalk](#/mechanisms/organelle-crosstalk)**: myelin contains cytoplasm-filled channels along which peroxisomes are carried by motor proteins, with traffic tuned to nerve activity, and losing the motor KIF21B stalled that traffic and led to axon degeneration in mice, a pattern also seen in aged mice and one the authors connect to multiple sclerosis ([Chapple 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42538476/))
furtherReading: [Gray 2014](https://doi.org/10.1177/1352458513505691) (reduced neuronal peroxisomes in MS grey matter)
[Chapple 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42538476/) (peroxisomes are transported along channels inside myelin; losing the motor causes axon degeneration in mice)
right: Can MS models be rescued by restoring peroxisomal function?
Which cell types are most sensitive to peroxisomal lipid dysfunction across neurodegenerative diseases?

parts.label: Parkinson's disease
parts.text: Reduced plasmalogens and altered peroxisomal function have been reported, but the evidence is thinner than for Alzheimer's or MS.
left: **[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens):](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis)** changes in brain and blood plasmalogens have been reported in Parkinson's disease, including reduced red blood cell and plasma plasmalogen species ([Mawatari 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35973579/)).

**[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens):](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis)** blood plasmalogens are lower in Parkinson's disease ([Dragonas 2009](https://doi.org/10.1515/cclm.2009.205)), and frontal cortex membrane lipids are altered ([Fabelo 2011](https://doi.org/10.2119/molmed.2011.00119)).

**[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens):](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis)** in MPTP mice, plasmalogen augmentation and plasmalogen precursors reduced striatal dopamine loss ([Miville-Godbout 2016](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0151020); [Miville-Godbout 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brainres.2017.08.020)). A causal role in human disease is not established.
furtherReading: [Mawatari 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35973579/) (reduced plasmalogen species in Parkinson's disease)
[Miville-Godbout 2016](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0151020) (plasmalogen augmentation reverses striatal dopamine loss in MPTP mice)
right: Direct evidence on whether peroxisomal dysfunction precedes or follows loss of dopamine-producing neurons.

parts.label: Vision and hearing loss
parts.text: Peroxisomes are needed to keep the retina and the inner ear working. Hair cells multiply their peroxisomes in response to sound, the retinal pigment epithelium depends on peroxisomal fat breakdown to clear its daily load, and vision and hearing loss are among the most consistent features when peroxisome function is lost.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)**: sound makes hair cells clear their peroxisomes and then build more; when this process is hindered, the cochlea (the organ that turns vibrations into electrical signals), becomes hypervulnerable to noise damage ([Delmaghani 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26544938/) and [Defourny 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30936319/)).

**[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown)**: the RPE (retinal pigment epithelium located at the back of the eye) requires peroxisomal beta-oxidation to maintain lysosomal function ([Kocherlakota 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37862382/)), and the lysosomal axis implicated in age-related macular degeneration.

**[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification)**: variation in the gene that encodes the peroxisomal enzyme catalase, is associated with noise-induced hearing loss in two independent noise-exposed populations ([Konings 2007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17567781/))
furtherReading: [Mardones 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26544930/) (commentary on peroxisomes and hearing loss)
right: Would enhancing peroxisomal function in the cochlea be a strategy to treat highly prevalent forms of hearing loss?

parts.label: Diabetic neuropathy
parts.text: In diabetic nerve damage, excess fat chemically modifies PEX11B so peroxisomes cannot divide, leaving fewer of them in Schwann cells, the cells that insulate peripheral nerves.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling) (division):** in diabetic mice and in Schwann cells exposed to palmitic acid, PEX11B is chemically modified so peroxisomes cannot elongate and divide, and peroxisome numbers fall; the PPARalpha agonist fenofibrate restored them ([Yang 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39934809/)).
furtherReading: [Yang 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39934809/) (excess fat modifies PEX11B so peroxisomes cannot divide in Schwann cells)
right: Is PEX11B modification the main link between fat overload and nerve damage in diabetic neuropathy?
Which PEX genes and formation steps are rate-limiting in fat cells, Schwann cells, beta-cells and key brain cell types?

label: Obesity & Diabetes
summary: Obesity and type 2 diabetes hinge on how fat is stored, released and burned for heat, and on whether the cells that make insulin survive
description: Obesity and type 2 diabetes hinge on how fat is stored, released and burned for heat, and on whether the cells that make insulin can survive.

parts.label: Obesity
parts.text: Peroxisome number rises as fat cells mature, and peroxisomes help decide when stored fat is released.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** as fat cells mature, peroxisome number and function increase ([Hofer 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28017862/)).

**[Biogenesis & Recycling:](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)** peroxisome formation is reduced in the white fat of obese mice, and individuals with obesity show lower expression of peroxisomal genes ([Piao 2019](https://doi.org/10.1089/ars.2018.7614)).

**[Biogenesis & Recycling:](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)** in mice, maternal obesity disrupted very long chain fatty acid storage in oocytes, impairing peroxisomal protein import in early embryos and derailing epigenetic reprogramming, with supporting data in human oocytes ([Zhang 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41851092/)).

**[Metabolic Signaling](#/mechanisms/metabolic-signaling):** high-fat diet reduced liver peroxisomal gene expression and fatty acid oxidation in mice, and the PPARalpha agonist fenofibrate restored both ([Jiang 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35746892/)).

**[Organelle Crosstalk](#/mechanisms/organelle-crosstalk):** during fasting, PEX5 delivers the fat-releasing enzyme ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contacts ([Han 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515256420960303)).

**[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification):** peroxisome-derived ROS stabilize PEX2, which degrades the fat-releasing enzyme ATGL and suppresses fat release ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).
furtherReading: [Jiang 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35746892/) (high-fat diet impairs liver peroxisomal biogenesis in mice; the PPARalpha agonist fenofibrate restores it)
[Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/) (peroxisome-derived ROS stabilize PEX2, which degrades ATGL and suppresses lipolysis)
[Lodhi and Semenkovich 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2014.01.002) (peroxisomes in lipid metabolism and signaling)
[Liu 2019](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.redox.2019.101167) (peroxisomal control of redox balance and adipocyte metabolism)
[Piao 2019](https://doi.org/10.1089/ars.2018.7614) (impaired peroxisomal fitness in obese mice)
[Zhang 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41851092/) (maternal obesity impairs peroxisomal import in early mouse embryos)
right: If peroxisome function is boosted during fat cell development, does that produce healthier fat cells?
In obesity and high insulin states, which steps in the peroxisome / lipid droplet / PEX5 / ATGL axis fail, and which can be safely restored?
How much does the peroxisome-specific PEX2-ATGL pathway, as opposed to mitochondrial fat burning, control lipid handling in obesity?
Which diet and exercise regimens best restore peroxisomal function, and does restoring it alone improve insulin resistance and inflammation?
Can boosting peroxisome formation or selective pexophagy reverse metabolic disease?

parts.label: Fat and energy expenditure
parts.text: White fat stores and releases energy; brown fat burns it to make heat. Peroxisomes are needed for both: fat cells cannot mature properly without them, and brown fat cannot make heat.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** silencing PEX16 in fat cells left them with fewer peroxisomes, slowed peroxisomal fat burning, and impaired the cells' ability to mature and store fat, with mitochondria unaffected ([Hofer 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28017862/)).

**[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** peroxisome-derived lipids are needed for cold-induced mitochondrial division in brown fat ([Park 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30511960/)).
**[Biogenesis & Recycling:](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling)** PEX13 is required for white fat to generate heat in cold-exposed mice ([Park 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34517131/)).
furtherReading: [Martens 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymgme.2012.10.015) (Pex5 knockout impairs white fat and muscle function)
[Park 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30511960/) (peroxisome-derived lipids drive cold-induced mitochondrial fission)
right: Which specific peroxisomal pathways in fat cells are required to protect against obesity and loss of heat generation?

parts.label: Insulin-producing beta-cells
parts.text: Functional peroxisomes are required for beta-cell integrity and insulin production.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** when peroxisomes fail, beta-cells die, even without obvious oxidative stress ([Baboota 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30795913/)).

**[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification)**: deleting Pex5 in mouse beta-cells raised insulin secretion yet worsened glucose control, with oxidized and truncated insulin and reduced maturity markers, indicating that peroxisomes protect insulin from oxidative damage ([Collier 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42378063/)).

**[Metabolic Signaling](#/mechanisms/metabolic-signaling):** genetic variants that activate PPARγ affect insulin sensitivity and diabetes risk ([Vales-Villamarin 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34887761/)).
furtherReading: [Baboota 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30795913/) (functional peroxisomes are required for beta-cell integrity and insulin production)
[Collier 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42378063/) (peroxisome loss in beta-cells yields oxidized insulin and worse glucose control)
right: Which peroxisomal pathway in beta-cells is necessary and sufficient to preserve their function?
How much of PPARγ's protective benefit happens through peroxisomal remodeling versus other targets?

label: Liver Disease
summary: Fatty liver disease, bile flow disorders and the liver damage of severe genetic peroxisomal disorders all involve two functions of liver peroxisomes: burning fats and building the bile acids that help the body absorb fats
description: Fatty liver disease, bile flow disorders and the liver damage of severe genetic peroxisomal disorders all involve two functions of liver peroxisomes: burning fats and building the bile acids that help the body absorb fats.

parts.label: Fatty liver disease (MASLD / MASH)
parts.text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and its inflammatory form MASH, are the most common chronic liver diseases.
left: **[Metabolic Signaling](#/mechanisms/metabolic-signaling):** the pan-PPAR agonist lanifibranor has been studied in clinical trials for MASH.

**[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** mice lacking the first enzyme of peroxisomal fat breakdown (ACOX1) develop fatty liver, inflammation and liver tumors ([Fan 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9624157/)).

**[Metabolic Signaling](#/mechanisms/metabolic-signaling):** high-fat diet impaired liver peroxisomal biogenesis and fatty acid oxidation in mice, and the PPARalpha agonist fenofibrate restored both and prevented liver injury, with no benefit in PPARalpha-deficient mice ([Jiang 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35746892/)).
furtherReading: [Jiang 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35746892/) (high-fat diet impairs liver peroxisomal biogenesis in mice; the PPARalpha agonist fenofibrate restores it)
right: How much of the benefit of PPAR drugs in MASH depends on peroxisomal fat burning versus mitochondrial or anti-inflammatory effects?
Does peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide contribute to liver injury in MASH?
Do PPAR drugs lose effectiveness when peroxisomal import or formation is impaired, and how does that dependency vary by tissue?

parts.label: Bile flow disorders (cholestatic liver disease)
parts.text: In cholestatic diseases, such as primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), bile does not flow normally and bile acids damage the liver.
left: **[Metabolic Signaling](#/mechanisms/metabolic-signaling):** two PPAR-targeting drugs, elafibranor and seladelpar, received accelerated FDA approval in 2024 for PBC.

**[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** peroxisomes perform the final steps of bile acid synthesis; whether those steps are altered in common cholestatic disease is not established. The evidence that exists is indirect, resting on PPAR drug effects on the bile acid pool rather than on direct measurement ([Ghonem 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32480421/)).
furtherReading: [Ghonem 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32480421/) (fibrates normalize the bile acid pool in patients responding partly to UDCA)
right: Do the PBC benefits of PPAR drugs involve peroxisomes at all?
Are peroxisome-specific bile acid intermediates useful biomarkers in cholestatic disease?

parts.label: Liver disease in genetic peroxisomal disorders
parts.panelTitle: Liver disease in genetic peroxisomal disorders
parts.text: Enlarged liver, impaired bile flow and scarring are common in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders and can progress to liver failure.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown):** 27-carbon bile acid intermediates accumulate. Oral cholic acid (FDA-approved 2015) is used as add-on treatment, with caution in advanced liver disease ([Berendse 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27469511/)).
furtherReading: [Braverman 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26750748/) (clinical overview of peroxisome biogenesis disorders)
right: Which peroxisomal functions drive liver injury in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders, and can liver-targeted therapy (for example liver-directed gene therapy) help even if brain disease is not addressed?

label: Kidney Disease
summary: Kidney stones, diabetic kidney damage and the cysts of Zellweger Spectrum Disorders each stem from a different peroxisomal dysfunction
description: Kidney stones, diabetic kidney damage and the cysts of Zellweger Spectrum Disorders each stem from a different peroxisomal dysfunction.

parts.label: Oxalate and kidney stone disease
parts.text: Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 is a peroxisomal disorder in which oxalate builds up and crystallizes in the kidneys.
left: **[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification):** loss of the peroxisomal enzyme AGXT lets glyoxylate turn into oxalate.

**[Biogenesis & Recycling](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** in some patients a working AGXT enzyme is sent to mitochondria instead of peroxisomes ([Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/)).
**Treatment:** lumasiran (FDA-approved 2020) reduces the function of glycolate oxidase, a peroxisomal enzyme upstream of oxalate ([Garrelfs 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33789010/)).
furtherReading: [Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/) (how AGT mistargeting causes primary hyperoxaluria type 1)
right: Genetic studies suggest the peroxisomal glyoxylate genes explain very little common stone disease: in 787 unselected adult kidney stone formers, variants in AGXT, GRHPR or HOGA1 were found in only three ([Anderegg 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38544324/)). Whether milder variation in this pathway contributes at all is still open.

parts.label: Diabetic kidney disease
parts.text: Diabetic kidneys develop peroxisomes that are structurally intact but functionally empty, and peroxisomal fat breakdown generates harmful by-products.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown) and [Organelle Crosstalk](#/mechanisms/organelle-crosstalk):** peroxisomal fat breakdown produces succinate, which disrupts mitochondrial energy production and generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) ([Wang 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8881667/)).
**[Detoxification](#/mechanisms/detoxification):** restoring the DsbA-L/catalase complex reduces kidney damage ([Liu 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213231723002562)).
furtherReading: [Wang 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8881667/) (peroxisomal fat breakdown produces succinate that damages the diabetic kidney)
[Liu 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213231723002562) (restoring the DsbA-L-catalase complex reduces kidney damage)
[Vasko 2016](https://doi.org/10.1089/ars.2016.6666) (peroxisomes and kidney injury)
right: Which molecules link peroxisomal fat breakdown to toxic succinate build-up and kidney damage?
Can established diabetic kidney disease be reversed by restoring the DsbA-L/catalase complex, or only slowed?
Could restoring peroxisomal ROS handling (for example, targeted catalase delivery or better protein import) improve brain, kidney, fat and muscle at the same time?

Whether boosting peroxisomal fat burning protects the kidney and heart during ischemia-reperfusion injury ([Gulati 1993](https://doi.org/10.1016/0925-4439%2893%2990071-8); [Liepinsh 2013](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00210-013-0849-0)).

parts.label: Kidney involvement in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders
parts.panelTitle: Kidney involvement in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders
parts.text: Kidney cysts and calcium oxalate stones occur in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders.
left: **[Detoxification:](#/mechanisms/detoxification)** hyperoxaluria is common in patients who survive past infancy, affecting 19 of 23 tested in one Dutch cohort, and five of 31 developed stones or nephrocalcinosis, one progressing to end-stage kidney disease ([van Woerden 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16621644/)).
furtherReading: [van Woerden 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16621644/) (hyperoxaluria and kidney involvement in Zellweger Spectrum Disorders patients)
right: Whether the screening proposed on the strength of one cohort, urinalysis for hyperoxaluria plus renal ultrasound, should become routine practice ([van Woerden 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16621644/)).

label: Aging
summary: Peroxisomes take in fewer enzymes, clear damage less well and lose contact with their neighbours as tissues age, the lipids they make and break down change with them, and in worms and yeast altering peroxisome function alters lifespan
description: Peroxisomes take in fewer enzymes, clear damage less well and lose contact with their neighbours as tissues age, the lipids they make and break down change with them, and in worms and yeast altering peroxisome function alters lifespan.

parts.label: Peroxisomal function declines with age and may contribute to aging itself
parts.panelTitle: Peroxisomal function declines with age and may contribute to aging itself
parts.text: With age, fewer enzymes reach the peroxisome, damaged ones are cleared away less effectively, and the contacts with neighboring compartments weaken. Animal studies suggest the relationship may run both ways: altering peroxisome function alters lifespan, so peroxisomal decline may be part of what drives aging itself.
left: **[Biogenesis & Recycling (import)](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** peroxisomal import declines with age in worms, mice and human cells, driven by the PEX5 receptor, and dietary restriction preserved peroxisomal function while raising prx-5 extended worm lifespan by up to about a quarter ([Sharma 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42162381/)).

**[Biogenesis & Recycling (division)](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** in C. elegans, blocking the peroxisome-fission protein PRX-11 prevented age-related pexophagy, preserved peroxisomes and youthful mitochondria and extended lifespan, so in this model less pexophagy rather than more was protective ([Flora 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40501931/)).

**[Biogenesis & Recycling (recycling)](#/mechanisms/biogenesis-recycling):** peroxisomal quality control that clears damaged peroxisomes weakens with age, so they accumulate as sources of oxidative damage ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Detoxification:](#/mechanisms/detoxification)** in worms and yeast, losing peroxisomal catalase shortens lifespan and produces premature-aging features ([Petriv 2004](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.m400207200)).

**[Organelle Crosstalk](#/mechanisms/organelle-crosstalk):** weaker contacts accelerate mitochondrial breakdown and muscle aging ([Scalabrin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64833-w)).
furtherReading: [Perichon 1998](https://doi.org/10.1007/s000180050192) (the role of peroxisomes in aging)
[Legakis 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12475949/) (peroxisome senescence in human fibroblasts)
[Koepke 2008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.taap.2008.06.004) (restoring catalase import reverses features of cellular aging)
[Cipolla 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5366081/) (peroxisomal dysfunction in age-related disease)
[Kim 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39398621/) (the peroxisomal import system declines with age)
right: What drives the age-dependent loss of peroxisomal import, and in which cell types?
Can restoring peroxisomal function in aged tissue reverse aging features, and would the effect be visible in blood?
Does failing quality control track with other markers of aging, and can enhancing selective pexophagy reverse tissue decline?
Can peroxisome contacts with other compartments be stabilized, and would that rescue age-related decline such as muscle loss?

parts.label: Peroxisomal lipids change with age in brain and blood
parts.panelTitle: Peroxisomal lipids change with age in brain and blood
parts.text: Peroxisomes both build lipids and break them down, and both sides of that ledger shift with age. Plasmalogens, the ether lipids peroxisomes build, fall in brain and blood, and the loss tracks with cognitive decline. How far peroxisomal function has dropped differs between tissues, and that pattern shows up in the blood lipid profile.
left: **[Lipid Breakdown](#/mechanisms/lipid-breakdown) and [Lipid Synthesis](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** tissue-specific peroxisomal decline is reflected in blood lipid profiles ([Vercaemst 2026](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/15/3/254)).

**[Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)](#/mechanisms/lipid-synthesis):** plasmalogen loss tracks with cognitive decline and influences cell-death sensitivity in aging tissues ([Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889)).
furtherReading: [Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889) (plasmalogens drop in brain and blood with age, tracking cognitive decline)
[Mi 2007](https://doi.org/10.1186/1477-5956-5-19) (age-related changes in mouse liver and kidney peroxisomes)
[Amelina 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jchromb.2011.08.044) (age-related changes in mouse liver peroxisomes)
[Narayan 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2016.06.011) (peroxisomal proteins that decline with age in C. elegans)
right: Which plasmalogen or ether lipid species in blood best predict functional aging, and could one panel serve aging, neurodegeneration and the ether lipid dependency seen in cancer?
What dosing range of plasmalogen replacement improves resilience without increasing harmful cell death?
